title: Residency enforcement — customer requirements notes (working doc)
content:
Purpose
- Capture customer asks and objections related to Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning) for Security & Compliance Foundation.
- Track competitor claims and how customers benchmark Redwood.
- Maintain open questions + decisions needed across Product/Security/Eng.

Owner / update cadence
- Owner: Naomi Feldman (Product — Security & Compliance)
- Updated ad hoc after customer calls + SE escalations. Please add sources/links when updating.

Executive summary (what customers keep asking for)
1) “EU-only means EU-only”
- Requests should never run outside EU regions, including during capacity events.
- Customers specifically call out: fallback behavior, background jobs, logging/tracing, and support access.

2) Clear enforcement + clear errors
- Customers want deterministic block behavior and actionable errors (not generic 500s).
- They need to be able to hand an error payload to their app team/SREs and immediately know what to change.

3) Control surface
- Common request: policy defined at org level with overrides at project and/or API key.
- Need a “primary region” plus “allowed regions” (e.g., primary=eu-central-1, allowed={eu-central-1, eu-west-1}).

4) Auditability
- Changes to residency settings must be auditable (who/when/what) with exportable logs.
- Customers want evidence for ISO/SOC2 narratives + procurement questionnaires.

5) APAC is rising
- More inbound asks for APAC-only pinning (Japan/Singapore/Australia) and “no US processing” language.
- Even when APAC-only is not mandatory, customers want the ability to keep APAC traffic in-region for latency and “data sovereignty expectations.”


Customer asks by theme (aggregated)

A) Residency scope — what is considered “customer content”
- Must remain in-region:
  - Prompt text, conversation history, system prompts, tool outputs that contain customer data
  - Uploaded documents (if/when supported via Hosted)
  - Model outputs (completions)
  - Fine-tuned model artifacts (future ask; mostly out of scope now but comes up)
- “Metadata allowed to move?”
  - Some customers accept limited cross-region metadata for billing/abuse prevention if content is excluded (need crisp explanation + contract language).
  - Repeated question: “Are request IDs, token counts, and error codes considered content?” (usually no, but must be documented).

B) Enforcement behavior / failure modes
- Hard block is preferred over silent reroute:
  - Many regulated customers want requests blocked if not routable in allowed region(s).
  - They do NOT want automatic cross-region fallback even if latency degrades.
- Capacity constraints:
  - “If EU region is down or full, do you fail closed?” (often yes for regulated workloads).
  - Some customers ask for a configurable mode: fail-closed vs fail-open (fail-open only if explicitly enabled and loudly signaled).

C) Configuration level + precedence
- Most common:
  - Org-level default policy
  - Project-level policy (override)
  - API key-level policy (tighten only, not broaden) — customers want least-privilege keys
- Precedence questions (needs a single consistent model):
  - If org=EU-only and a project tries to set US-only → should be rejected
  - If org=EU-only and key tries EU+US → should be rejected
  - If org=EU+UK and key narrows to EU-only → allowed

D) Error messaging / developer experience
- Common requirements:
  - Stable HTTP status for residency blocks
  - Machine-readable error_code
  - Request ID echoed back
  - A help URL to docs + a short “how to fix” (e.g., “Update project residency policy to include region X, or send request to the EU endpoint.”)
- Streaming endpoints:
  - Customers have seen other vendors return mid-stream errors poorly; they explicitly ask what happens if a policy evaluation fails after stream starts.

E) Observability + audit logs
- Customer asks:
  - View blocked requests in console (at least last 7–30 days)
  - Reason codes for blocks (e.g., region_not_allowed, no_capacity_in_allowed_regions)
  - Audit logs for policy changes with actor identity
  - Export to SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, Sumo Logic)

F) Dedicated vs Hosted expectations
- Dedicated buyers generally assume region residency is “easier” (single tenant), but still ask:
  - Is control plane regional?
  - Are operational logs content-bearing?
  - Is support access and debugging constrained to region?
- Hosted buyers need stricter explanations:
  - Multi-tenant control plane, but runtime/routing must enforce boundaries.


Customer snapshots (specific accounts / notes)

1) Nordholm Payments (regulated payments; EU-only)
- Source: HubSpot record + Feb 4 security review call transcript
- Key asks / objections:
  - Must guarantee “no US processing” for prompts and outputs
  - Wants audit log export of residency policy changes
  - Wants deterministic statement on failover: “Do not failover outside EU; block instead.”
  - Wants evidence pack content: architecture statement + control mapping (SOC2)
- Open items from Nordholm:
  - Clarify whether any support tooling (tracing) can pull content outside the region
  - Provide sample error payload for their integration team

2) Helix Health Systems (healthcare platform; evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated)
- Source: HubSpot record
- Key asks:
  - EU-only for some tenants; US-only for others (multi-tenant SaaS)
  - Wants project-level separation (per tenant) with distinct API keys
  - Wants “data processing location” language for their BAAs / DPAs
  - Wants to know if any logs contain PHI (answer must be “no”; if risk exists, needs mitigation)
- Notes:
  - They’re open to Dedicated if Hosted cannot meet the required assurances in time, but prefer Hosted for speed.

3) DACH procurement / legal (multiple prospects; recurring theme)
- Source: Hannah Schmitt procurement email thread
- Key asks:
  - Contract language specifying region(s) and incident notification if residency is violated
  - Subprocessor region list and whether subprocessors have access to content
  - Right to audit / evidence artifacts available on request

4) APAC pinning (Japan/Singapore/Australia)
- Source: multiple inbound asks via SE, not all logged yet
- Common asks:
  - Pinning for APAC traffic for sovereignty + latency
  - “No US or EU processing” depending on the customer
  - Need clarity on which APAC regions are supported and whether model catalog differs by region


Competitor comparisons (what customers reference)

What customers cite as “baseline” expectations
- “Pin the region, do not move content across regions.”
- “Console setting and audit log of changes.”
- “Contractual commitments + subprocessor transparency.”

Competitors named (non-exhaustive)
- Hyperscalers: AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI
- API providers: OpenAI, Anthropic
- Inference platforms: Together, Fireworks, Groq (more latency-focused, less compliance depth in some deals)

Observed competitor positioning (from customer paraphrases; validate before quoting)
- “Azure gives region selection, but cross-region behaviors are complicated; support answers vary.”
- “Bedrock is the easiest for procurement because it inherits AWS region controls, but model availability differs by region.”
- “Some API vendors say ‘we process in-region’ but can’t explain logging/tracing boundaries.”

Where Redwood can win (based on customer feedback)
- Crisp enforcement boundaries + deterministic behavior, especially around fallback.
- Better troubleshooting: clear error codes + blocked-request views.
- Evidence pack that maps product behavior to controls (SOC2/ISO) without hand-wavy language.


Open questions / decisions needed

Policy model + precedence
- Do we allow API key policies to broaden beyond project/org? (current leaning from security: NO; allow narrowing only)
- What is the canonical precedence order? Proposal:
  - Org policy sets maximum allowed region set
  - Project policy must be subset of org allowed set
  - API key policy must be subset of project allowed set

Failover modes
- Should we support explicit “fail-open (allow cross-region) with audit event” as a future option?
  - Pros: uptime for non-regulated
  - Cons: procurement risk, accidental misconfig; harder to explain

Endpoints + “which URL do I call?”
- Do we require region-specific base URLs (eu.api.redwood.ai) or keep a global URL with internal routing?
  - Customers are split: regulated teams like explicit endpoints; developers like global.
  - If global URL remains, we need to be extra clear that routing never exits allowed regions.

Logs/traces boundary
- Confirm and document:
  - Which telemetry fields are content-bearing
  - Which systems store or emit payloads
  - How sampling and debug logging are handled under incident response

Evidence pack contents
- What minimum set of artifacts do we standardize for enterprise security reviews?
  - Architecture diagram
  - Control narrative
  - Audit event schema examples
  - Dashboard screenshots / metric definitions


Action items (near-term)
- Naomi: add 2–3 crisp “customer-safe” FAQ answers on failover + logs/traces boundaries (coordinate with Marcus/Olga).
- Markus/Avery: make sure Nordholm gets sample error payload + timeline expectations; collect any additional redline language.
- Elliot/Wei: incorporate common asks into public docs outline (region pinning + troubleshooting) once ADR-022 is finalized.

Notes from recent calls (raw)

2025-02-04 — Security review: data residency + audit logs
- Customer: Nordholm Payments
- Participants: Markus Klein (SE), Avery Johnson (AE), Marcus Lin (Security Eng), Naomi Feldman (Product)
- Raw takeaways:
  - They asked 4 times whether “fallback will go to US.” This is the #1 blocker.
  - Audit logs: need actor identity, timestamp, previous vs new values, and export mechanism.
  - They need written confirmation of what “content” includes.

2025-02-18 — POC scoping: EU-only Hosted API
- Customer: (prospect; name in transcript)
- Participants: Markus Klein, Mina Haddad (Routing), Naomi Feldman
- Raw takeaways:
  - They will test forced capacity failure to see if we fail closed.
  - They want to pin at per-environment granularity (staging vs prod) using separate projects and keys.

Appendix — terminology (draft)
- Primary region: preferred region within allowed set for routing decisions.
- Allowed regions: the only regions where customer content may be processed.
- Residency violation: request cannot be satisfied within allowed regions under current configuration and capacity, so it is blocked (unless an explicit override exists).

Changelog
- 2025-02-05: initial draft created (Naomi)
- 2025-02-21: added DACH procurement requirements and APAC notes (Hannah/Markus)
- 2025-03-01: expanded competitor section + clarified recurring asks for per-key narrowing (Naomi/Marcus)
